rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – criminal record screening restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, in writing or orally, before making a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications. After a conditional offer, they may consider only certain serious convictions and indictable offenses within lookback periods of 6, 4 or 1 years depending on the degree of the offense. Any withdrawal of an offer requires an individualized assessment, written notice and a chance to appeal, and housing providers may not require drug or alcohol tests.
rules.key_value: No criminal record inquiry before conditional offer; lookback 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd degree), 1 yr (4th degree)

exemption_conditions.condition: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded from the definition of rental dwelling unit

coverage.notes: The owner-occupied exemption applies only to premises with 4 or fewer dwelling units. Housing providers may consider methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration at any stage.

rules.coverage_text: Applies to housing providers (landlords, owners, lessors, sublessors, assignees or their agents) for dwelling units offered for rent for residential purposes.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are excluded. Before a conditional offer, providers may still consider convictions for methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration requirements.
rules.interaction: Does not bar rights or actions that exist independently, including under P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.). Notwithstanding the Anti-Eviction Act, a housing provider that wins an appeal may evict an applicant housed under a director's order, with at least 45 days' notice. Landlords subject to the act are immune from civil liability for renting to people with criminal records.

tool_input.notes: I recorded one rule: New Jersey's Fair Chance in Housing Act (P.L. 2021, c.110). Its criminal record and drug or alcohol test limits on screening are grouped into this single rule. The effective date of 2022-01-01 is derived from the stated formula and the approval date of June 18, 2021. The disclosure required before accepting an application fee is part of the criminal record screening rules, so I did not record it as a separate rule.
